jobs.title: Director of Engineering (Utility-Scale Solar & BESS)
jobs.description:
This role is based in Arlington, VA. On-site presence is required.

About the Company

Join a leading independent power producer at the forefront of renewable energy development. With a growing portfolio of utility-scale solar projects across Virginia, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, and Kentucky, our client develops, constructs, owns, and operates renewable energy assets backed by a 7GW+ global pipeline and over 1GW already commissioned.

The Role

We are hiring a Director of Engineering who will be based at the Arlington, Virginia headquarters. This role leads and manages an engineering team supporting projects involving utility-scale solar facilities, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and related generation tie lines and substations. It oversees engineering design activities, coordination with third-party consultants and contractors, and the delivery of technical support throughout project development, procurement, construction, and commissioning.

The engineering group manages civil and electrical design scopes, conducts design reviews to enhance system performance and reduce costs, and develops standardized, repeatable design solutions for future projects. The Director also provides technical leadership to internal teams including Development, M&A;, Construction, Operations Engineering, Compliance, and Asset Management, while establishing team objectives, workflows, and operating procedures.

Key Responsibilities

Lead a multidisciplinary team of civil and electrical engineers and technical specialists
Continuously improve engineering design management processes
Forecast staffing needs based on active projects and future pipeline, and assign resources to support development and construction activities
Identify long-term resource requirements and recruit project engineering personnel
Act as a senior technical authority supporting development, M&A, and construction efforts, and manage external subject-matter experts as required
Review and resolve complex technical issues in collaboration with internal experts and external consultants
Develop and implement efficient engineering workflows focused on standardization and repeatable designs
Provide technical coordination with Operations Engineering, Development, Compliance, and Asset Management teams at various project stages
Ensure regulatory and compliance requirements, including NERC standards, are incorporated into project designs
Lead technical coordination with lenders' independent engineers during design and construction phases
Periodic site visits as required

Education and Experience

Bachelor's degree in engineering required; electrical engineering preferred
Professional Engineering License
8 years + of experience in the energy industry
Minimum of 5 years of experience in utility-scale solar project engineering; BESS experience is a plus
Experience working in PJM and MISO markets is a plus
Background in civil and electrical design, medium-voltage collection systems, high-voltage substations, and SCADA for utility-scale solar projects
Experience supporting construction and commissioning activities
Experience preparing or reviewing construction cost estimates for similar projects

Work Location, Remote Work, and Travel

This position will be based in Arlington, VA. Travel may be required over time.

jobs.title: Director, Infrastructure & Cloud Practice
jobs.description:
Director, Infrastructure & Cloud Practice

WE ARE GROWING

Provisions Group is looking to bring on a Director, Infrastructure & Cloud Practice to join our IT Professional Services team.

This is a 100% remote Full Time opportunity. You’ll be working directly with our clients in a consulting environment.
Please note we are not able to partner with third party staffing firms on this role. Candidates must be able to work directly with Provisions Group.

Position Summary

The Director of Infrastructure & Cloud Practice leads a multidisciplinary practice of more than 20 engineers, ensuring the organization has the people, capabilities, processes, and service offerings necessary to deliver consistent client outcomes.

This leader is accountable for coordinating pre-sales solution development, overseeing the quality of statements of work, aligning staffing and skills with business demand, maintaining an efficient work intake process, developing repeatable service offerings, and establishing consistent delivery standards.

The role requires strong technical judgment, particularly in Azure architecture, Microsoft Modern Work and related licensing, DevOps practices, and solution design. This is a leadership and oversight position with limited hands-on implementation.

Must Haves

You have led multidisciplinary engineering teams in a consulting or multi-client environment balancing competing client demands, developing technical talent, and staying accountable for delivery.
You bring strong technical judgment across infrastructure and cloud, including Azure architecture, Modern Work and licensing, DevOps practices, and infrastructure design. You can challenge assumptions and involve the right experts.
You have guided solutions from discovery through delivery handoff, coordinating presales contributors, shaping estimates, and reviewing SOWs to ensure scope, assumptions, risks, and deliverables are clear before work is committed.
You can build a consistent practice operating model, improving capacity planning, work intake and prioritization, delivery standards, and repeatable services.

Core Responsibilities

1. Pre-Sales Coordination & Solution Oversight
Coordinate the right contributors.
Partner with sales to identify the disciplines and specialists needed for discovery, solution design, and estimation.
Provide solution oversight.
Guide technical direction, challenge assumptions, and ensure proposed solutions address client objectives, architectural fit, licensing, operational requirements, and delivery risks.
Oversee statement-of-work quality.
Establish review and approval processes so SOWs contain clear scope, deliverables, assumptions, exclusions, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and realistic effort estimates.

2. Staffing, Capacity & Skills Management
Plan capacity against demand.
Provide oversight of capacity and capability planning.
Manage practice capabilities.
Maintain an actionable view of skills, proficiency, certifications, and subject matter expertise.
Lead and develop the organization.
Set clear performance expectations and ensure effective coaching, feedback, and career development.

3. Work Intake & Prioritization
Own the practice intake process.
Define how requests enter the queue, what information is required, who evaluates them, and how they move toward assignment.
Create clear prioritization and assignment rules.
Coordinate competing demands across sales, projects, and service operations.
Maintain queue visibility and accountability.
Track ownership, status, aging, blocked requests, and assignment delays.

4. Productized Services & Offering Development
Own the offering roadmap.
Identify and prioritize opportunities for assessments, maintenance packages, advisory services, modernization engagements, and other repeatable offerings.
Define complete service packages.
Ensure each offering has a clear target customer, intended outcome, scope, deliverables, exclusions, delivery approach, required skills, effort model, and pricing inputs.
Coordinate development and improvement.
Assign subject matter experts to develop technical methods, templates, and delivery assets.

5. Consistent Team Output & Technical Standards
Define what good delivery looks like.
Establish expectations for solution designs, implementation plans, technical documentation, testing evidence, operational handoffs, and client-facing deliverables.
Build quality into the process.
Use technical leads and subject matter experts to conduct design reviews, peer reviews, and delivery checkpoints.
Address recurring performance issues.
Monitor avoidable rework, estimation variance, incomplete deliverables, documentation gaps, and client concerns.

Technical Leadership Profile

• Azure architecture:
Evaluate architectural approaches, guide modernization decisions, and challenge designs for security, reliability, operability, and cost.
• Modern Work and licensing:
Guide solution discussions and ensure proposed capabilities, licensing assumptions, and commercial implications are validated by the appropriate experts.
• DevOps practices:
Establish expectations for automation, version control, deployment discipline, review practices, and repeatable engineering processes.
• Solution design:
Translate business objectives into a coherent solution approach and ensure contributions from multiple disciplines fit together.

Required Experience & Qualifications

Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary engineering teams in a consulting, professional services, managed services, or comparable multi-client environment.
Strong technical judgment in Azure architecture, Modern Work, DevOps practices, and infrastructure solution design.
Experience coordinating pre-sales discovery, technical solutioning, estimation, SOW review, and handoffs into delivery.
Proven ability to manage capacity, develop technical talent, improve work intake, and establish consistent engineering standards.
Experience developing repeatable service offerings, with an understanding of service packaging, delivery effort, resource utilization, and profitability.
Strong communication, delegation, and cross-functional leadership skills.

Measures of Success

• Pre-sales solutioning and SOW oversight

The right experts are engaged early, responsibilities are clear, and delivery commitments are complete and achievable.
Measures: Solutioning and SOW turnaround time; review completion; avoidable SOW rework; delivery issues tied to discovery or scoping gaps.

• Staffing and skills management

Staffing and capabilities support committed work and anticipated demand without persistent overload or critical single-person dependencies.
Measures: Capacity forecast accuracy; staffing delays; critical-skill coverage; development-plan progress; workload balance.

• Work intake efficiency

Requests are visible, sufficiently defined, prioritized, and assigned without unnecessary delay.
Measures: Time to triage and assignment; aged or unowned requests; blocked-work duration; adherence to the intake process.

• Service offerings

Assessments, maintenance packages, and other services are clearly packaged, delivery-ready, and used by sales and delivery teams.
Measures: Offerings launched and adopted; repeatability of delivery; offering revenue and margin; client feedback.

• Consistent team output

Teams produce reliable, complete, and professionally presented work across disciplines and engagements.
Measures: Quality-review results; avoidable rework; documentation completeness; delivery predictability; client satisfaction.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Technology Officer - Lifecor
Lifecor is a startup technology-driven life insurance carrier in formation, initially focused on term and final expense products.

We are building a company that sits at the intersection of insurance, technology, underwriting, distribution, data, and capital. We are currently working through carrier acquisition, reinsurance, product development, and distribution while assembling the small group of people who will define what Lifecor becomes.

The technology opportunity is enormous.

The systems built today will ultimately touch nearly every part of the company: how customers buy insurance, how agents submit business, how risks are underwritten, how policies are issued and administered, how data moves through the organization, and how AI and automation are deployed across the carrier.

The CTO will have the ability to shape that entire technology platform while earning meaningful ownership in the company.

NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS
Can you figure things out without being told how?
Do you work harder than others?
Are you talented? 1 + 1 = 2.

If you believe, or even think for a second, that your answer is no for ANY of these questions, do not apply. We are not the right fit.

You should be capable of:
Building and shipping product yourself
Designing scalable architecture
Leveraging AI aggressively across the organization
Integrating underwriting, carrier, distribution, and data systems
Solving difficult technical problems quickly
Recruiting exceptionally talented engineers
Taking complete ownership of the technology organization

You will have direct responsibility for Lifecor’s technology architecture, product development, engineering organization, AI strategy, and technical execution as the company scales.

Lifecor is not yet capitalized, so this role currently offers no cash compensation
; meaningful equity is available, and if you are not willing to work for equity until we are funded, do not apply.

Questions? Email cfeiner@lifecor.us.

Executive

Full-time

Industries

Insurance
